invariants.invariant: publish_environment never touches the world environment while the executor owns it and is still running
playbook: publish_environment refuses when _world_environment is set and execution_has_stopped() is false.
This is an API-order guard, not a data error: stop the executor or use the executor's own environment path before publishing.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the host environment test.

invariants.invariant: A restored climate view publishes the hash of the state that was installed.
initialize_world_environment runs only while the executor is stopped
playbook: initialize_world_environment refuses when !execution_has_stopped().
Because the seed is moved in, publishing it mid-execution would tear the per-cell arrays the running stages read; stop the executor first.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the host environment test.

invariants.invariant: every per-cell array in the environment seed carries exactly cell_count entries
playbook: initialize_world_environment refuses when the seed's per-cell arrays (including military_base_landform) disagree with seed.cell_count.
Compare the seed builder's cell count with the terrain the host already holds; a terrain resize without re-seeding produces this.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the host environment test.

invariants.invariant: a climate calendar checkpoint in a restore bundle decodes and applies completely
playbook: initialize_world_environment refuses when _world_environment->restore_calendar on the pending bundle's climate_calendar_bytes returns false.
Check the bundle's byte length against the calendar version the climate store expects; a bundle written by an older layout fails here rather than midway through the restore.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the climate restore test.

invariants.invariant: every era reward modifier key hash resolves to a definition loaded in _modifier_definition_id_by_key_hash
playbook: service_era_reward_requests refuses when the requested key hash is absent from _modifier_definition_id_by_key_hash.
Compare the reward's modifier key with the definitions the modifier catalog published for this epoch.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the era reward test.

invariants.invariant: an era reward modifier batch is accepted by enqueue_batch_at on the day it was built
playbook: service_era_reward_requests sets this when error is still empty and enqueue_batch_at refuses the packet batch.
Check the executor state and the batch size the reward produced; a batch built for a domain that is not accepting packets is the usual cause.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the era reward test.

invariants.invariant: a completed narrative effect that reports not-ok carries a reason; the stage supplies this id rather than finishing silently
playbook: stage_narrative sets this when the effect request completes with ok=false and an empty error.
Reproduce the day and inspect the narrative effect return: an economy application that failed without a code is the usual cause.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the narrative effect test.

invariants.invariant: a decoded country command matches its envelope (opcode and payload shape) before it enters the plan
playbook: decode_command refuses when the payload does not match the envelope, including command.opcode != envelope.opcode.
Compare the sender's opcode with the envelope it stamped; a mismatch means two encoders disagree on the layout.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the country pod command test.

invariants.invariant: committed investment leg capital >= required_capital: carried (drained-sponsor branch) or carried plus sponsor correction (capital top-up branch) never drops below the leg minimum
playbook: Read fatal_context_report()'s investment row: branch (1 = drained sponsor, 2 = capital top-up), cell, type_id, portfolio_index/portfolio_size.
Compare carried and correction against required_capital: branch 1 fails when carried < required_capital, branch 2 when sponsor_funds < correction.

Check the investment_legs trace per leg (allocated, carried, correction, credit, owner_funds_at_material); a leg whose carried claim vanished points at move_cohort_population, a short sponsor pool points at find_entrepreneur_source.
Re-run the failing day with the economy invariant probe fixture for the same cell/type before touching ledger order or funding rules.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the economy invariant probe suite, and keep the flat investment_row keys in fatal_context_report().

invariants.invariant: market lane stock >= planned material quantity for every good in the construction material plan at construction commit time
playbook: Read fatal_context_report()'s construction row: cell, type_id, first_good_id, first_required, first_stock, good_count.
The commit loop failed on stock[market, good] < planned_quantities[i]; compare the preflight material plan (good_ids/quantities) with the lane stock read at commit.
Look for a same-epoch consumer of the same (market, good) lane between preflight and commit (production input purchase, maintenance, army lane pay) and for merchant restock ordering.
Re-run the day with the probe fixture for that cell; do not tolerate negative stock or clip the plan to hide the drift.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus building commit tests.

invariants.invariant: committed owner funds >= material_plan.total_cost at construction invoice time
playbook: Read fatal_context_report()'s construction row: owner_slot, owner_funds, total_cost, funding_gap, debt_principal, material_feasible.

Recompute the preflight projection for that owner: funds at plan time must cover total_cost; a mismatch means funds moved between preflight and invoice (tax settlement, subsidy, another construction leg).
Check the funding legs that were supposed to cover the invoice: funding_capital + merchant_credit >= total_cost, and whether material_plan.feasible flipped after the plan was built.
Re-run with the economy invariant probe fixture for that cell/type; do not relax the preflight or fall back to silently skipping the build.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the economy suite, keeping the flat construction_row keys.

invariants.invariant: a family expedition target key (country, target) is pending at most once; a second start for the same target is refused instead of double-booking the destination
playbook: apply_start_family_expedition refuses when _family_expedition_target_index already holds family_expedition_target_key(country, target).

Check the caller for a UI retry or a re-entered day that resubmits the same expedition; the index releases on completion/cancel, so a stale entry means the previous expedition never released its target.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the colonization expedition test.

invariants.invariant: a continuation checkpoint that declares a pending structure section carries exactly structural_fields rows and a fully consumed cursor
playbook: EconomyAuthorityTransfer::restore_continuations refuses when structure_present is true but in.rows(pending, structural_fields) fails or in.cursor != in.size().
Compare the writer and the reader field list for the pending structure section: one extra or missing field leaves the cursor short of the section end.
A save written before structural_fields changed will trip this; re-save from a clean session rather than relaxing the check.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the continuation checkpoint round-trip test.

invariants.invariant: a family trait command names a live family handle and a non-negative day before its strength is validated
playbook: resolve_family_trait_command refuses when families_store().valid_handle(handle, family) fails or day < 0.
A family merged or extinguished earlier in the same day makes a queued trait command stale; re-issue it after the family commit instead of retrying the same handle.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the family trait narrative tests.

invariants.invariant: a family trait command strength lies within the catalog range and lands exactly on the trait's strength step grid
playbook: resolve_family_trait_command refuses when strength is out of range for the trait id or (strength - minimum) % _family_trait_strength_step_q16[id] != 0.

Read the trait catalog row for the requested id and compare minimum/step against the value the UI sent; the grid check is exact on purpose, so an off-grid value is a caller bug, not a rounding problem.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the family trait narrative tests.

invariants.invariant: every building maintenance exception record in a save names an existing row and a non-negative paid amount
playbook: The reader refuses when row >= records or paid < 0 while decoding the maintenance exception block.
Compare the block's declared record count with the building row count the same save declares; a mismatch means writer and reader disagree on the block layout.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the save round-trip test.

invariants.invariant: a market signal observation block's declared element count never exceeds the value array the same section reserved
playbook: The reader refuses when read_le(bytes, cursor, size) fails or size > values->size().
A truncated save or a layout change without a version bump produces this; compare the declared count against the array length the section reserved.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the save round-trip test.

invariants.invariant: a builtin transaction id appears at most once when the effect snapshot is built; a repeat is remapped, never silently dropped
playbook: The builder refuses when next_transaction_ids already contains row.transaction.id.
Find the producer that reused a builtin id: colonization and ideology builtin transactions allocate from different bases, so a collision means one producer ignored its base.
Confirm the remap path still emits the CLAIM/SETTLE pair for the remapped row before treating the collision as cosmetic.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the effect transaction id test.

invariants.invariant: an incoming ideology transaction that reuses an existing id carries the same plan_hash; a different plan is a collision, not a duplicate
playbook: The builder refuses when the id is already present and incoming.plan_hash != row.transaction.plan_hash.
Recompute plan_hash for the incoming transaction; a differing hash means two different plans were allocated the same id.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the effect transaction id test.

invariants.invariant: applying a narrative economy effect requires a bound _economy_production_runtime
playbook: The narrative effect path refuses when _economy_production_runtime is null.
Check the host wiring order: the economy production runtime has to be bound before the narrative stage runs, which is a bootstrap problem rather than a data problem.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the narrative effect test.

invariants.invariant: the effect transport refuses a packet once a stop was requested outside the day boundary
playbook: This id is raised by the host effect self-test (fail("...")), not by production code: request_stop() followed by enqueue(packet) must be refused.
If it fires, the stop gate is evaluated after admission; inspect the request_stop path in the effect transport rather than the test.
Kind is unknown on purpose: a failing self-test assertion is not a runtime refusal, and promoting it to fatal would need an assert id this path does not have.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the host effect transport test.

invariants.invariant: the effect transport refuses a packet after a stop request while no day is in flight
playbook: Raised by the host effect self-test: request_stop() with no inflight day, then enqueue(packet), must be refused.
If it fires, the idle-executor branch of the stop gate is missing; compare with the _worker_day_inflight branch of the same test.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the host effect transport test.

invariants.invariant: a packet admitted while a country command is in flight survives the stop and is not dropped
playbook: Raised by the host effect self-test when stopping->enqueue(packet) returns false under AtomicCounterScope day(stopping->_worker_day_inflight).
An in-flight day must keep admitting packets that already belong to it; if it drops them the country command loses its effect.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the host effect transport test.

invariants.invariant: queuing a military command never dereferences a missing dependency: a null economy runtime / runtime host / country state, or a missing worker frame while the executor is active, refuses the row with this reason instead
playbook: Read the refused batch row (caller_sequence, op, country, cell): this reason means the queue ran before the military executor was wired, not that the player's input was wrong.

Inspect _economy_runtime, _runtime_host and country_state on the NativeMilitaryRuntime that produced the row; any of them null is the direct cause, and so is a missing worker frame while _runtime_host->military_executor_active() is true.
Check the world-extension bootstrap order: the economy runtime has to be bound before the first military command batch of the day is queued.
If the frame is only missing on some days while the wiring is complete, suspect the worker boundary handoff (frame publication vs command queue) rather than the wiring.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the military construction queue test.

invariants.invariant: every MilitaryStateBuilding row carries a non-negative economy_building_id, and every requested state-building type resolves to a catalog row on an in-range cell
playbook: Read the refused row: type is the requested economy building id and cell is the target cell. Preflight also returns this reason for a cell outside core().terrain().cell_count, so check the range before blaming the catalog.

Look the type up in core().catalog().state_buildings: a missing row means the catalog does not define that state building, and a row with economy_building_id < 0 means the mapping to the economy building type was never filled in for that catalog entry.
Fix the catalog data that fills economy_building_id, not the queue: queue_player_construction must not silently skip an unmapped state building.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the military state building catalog test.

invariants.invariant: a country-bound military command batch is either enqueued whole or reported back with this reason
playbook: submit_military_country_commands sets this when _runtime_host->enqueue_batch refuses the packet batch.
Check the executor state the batch was built against (stopped/running) and the batch size limit.
The Godot side receives the same code through the receipt dictionary (submitted.code/reason), so one id covers both surfaces.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the military receipt test.

invariants.invariant: a military terrain checkpoint holds exactly 5 bytes per terrain cell
playbook: restore_terrain refuses when bytes.size() != cells * 5.
Read the cell count from the same checkpoint header and multiply by the record size; a terrain resize without a save migration produces this.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the military terrain restore test.

invariants.invariant: every element of a submitted military command batch is a Dictionary
playbook: submit_military_commands sets the row error when batch[i] is not Variant::DICTIONARY.
The other rows of the same batch still run, so read the whole receipt array: a single malformed element does not abort the batch.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the military command submit test.

invariants.invariant: a PKMI budget policy section declares a consistent row count, exactly n*12 payload bytes, and upkeep bp within [0,10000]
playbook: The reader raises this at three points: section_remaining() < sizeof(uint32_t), n != policies.size() or section_remaining() != n*12, and budget_upkeep_bp outside [0,10000].
Compare the writer's record size with the reader's 12-byte expectation and check the policy count the section header declares.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the PKMI budget save round-trip test.

invariants.invariant: every serialized family expedition person handle resolves to a live notable person whose cohort handle is 0 and whose family handle equals the expedition's family handle
playbook: Read the restore rejection reason reported by set_restore_rejected_reason() together with the PKEC family-expedition section cursor: the person lane of one expedition payload was rejected.

The assertion has two triggers: a serialized person handle of 0, or a live slot whose cohort handle is non-zero / family handle differs from the expedition family. A dead handle is already dropped into _restore.dropped_transit_persons, so a stop here is the attribution mismatch case.

Dump the save's person lane and the restored persons_store() rows for that handle: cohort_handle, family_handle, and the expedition family, then decide whether the lane is orphaned or the family attribution is wrong.
Fix the producing side (who wrote a person into the expedition lane) or, when the lane is genuinely orphaned, drop it explicitly and count it; never zero the lane silently.
Regression: PKEC save/restore round-trip test plus python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict.

invariants.invariant: a family claim transaction the save lists as pending is still present and not ACKED when the snapshot is rebuilt
playbook: The restore path fails when a family claim candidate's transaction_status_pod(6) is already ACKED while the save still lists it pending.
Compare the save's pending set with the replayed effect queue: an ack that ran without the save being rewritten produces exactly this pair of states.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the effect pod restore test.

invariants.invariant: colonization transaction ids stay below BUILTIN_TRANSACTION_ID_BASE so the builtin id range stays disjoint
playbook: The restore path fails when colo_tx_id < BUILTIN_TRANSACTION_ID_BASE.
Check the colonization allocator: it has to count up from the builtin base, not from zero.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the effect pod restore test.

invariants.invariant: building or restoring the effect snapshot never loses a pending family colonization transaction
playbook: The path fails when the rebuilt candidate reports no pending family colonization transactions while the source still had them.
Diff the pending set before and after the snapshot build for the same day.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the effect snapshot test.

invariants.invariant: every pending colonization transaction id resolves to an index in the candidate queue
playbook: The path fails when transaction_index_for_id(colo_tx_id) returns a negative index.
Confirm the id was inserted with the same base and that the queue was not rebuilt from a shorter list.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the effect pod restore test.

invariants.invariant: the collision-remap path ends with as many pending colonization transactions as it started with
playbook: The path fails when the colliding-colonization branch leaves the candidate without the pending family colonization transactions the source had.
Trace the remapped id through the queue after the collision; a remap that writes the new id but forgets the pending row is the usual cause.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the effect snapshot test.

invariants.invariant: a remapped colonization transaction id is registered exactly once in _native_country_bound_transaction_ids
playbook: The path fails when _native_country_bound_transaction_ids.count(resolved_id) != 1.
Check the remap table for a duplicate insert or for an entry written under the old id.
Regression: python tools/ci/check_fault_taxonomy.py --strict plus the effect snapshot test.

invariants.invariant: The confirmation section must decode completely before the runtime bundle can be queued for restore.
